questions.question: In the one-dimensional 0/1 knapsack, why must the capacity loop run from high to low?
options: It is faster because of CPU caching
So that dp[c - w] still holds the value from before the current item, ensuring each item is used at most once
Because the answer is stored in dp[0]
Looping upwards causes an infinite loop
questions.explanation: Going downwards means dp[c - w] has not yet been updated for the current item. Looping upwards lets an item be added repeatedly, which solves the unbounded knapsack instead.

questions.question: In the O(n log n) LIS algorithm, what does the `tails` array represent?
options: The input sorted in ascending order
tails[k] is the smallest possible tail value of an increasing subsequence of length k + 1
The indices where the sequence decreases
questions.explanation: tails stays sorted, so each element is placed by binary search. Only its length is meaningful; it is not necessarily an actual subsequence of the input.

questions.question: In LCS, when a[i-1] !== b[j-1], what is dp[i][j]?
questions.explanation: On a mismatch, drop the last character of one string or the other and take the better result. Resetting to 0 is the rule for longest common substring, not subsequence.

questions.question: In interval DP such as matrix-chain multiplication, in what order should the table be filled?
options: Row by row from top to bottom
Column by column from left to right
By increasing interval length, so all shorter ranges are ready before longer ones
questions.explanation: dp[i][j] depends on dp[i][k] and dp[k+1][j], which are shorter intervals. Filling by length guarantees those are already computed.
